text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- The government proposes the postponement of VAT for a year until January 1, 1988.
- President Tudjman visits the Croatian embassy in Washington to launch the English edition of his book "The Horrors of War".
- The U.S. warship in the port of Ploce begins unloading arms for the Bosnian federation.
- Thousands gather peacefully in the centre of Zagreb in support of independent Radio 101.
- Private Kaptol Banka plans to increase capital for expansion.
- Radio 101 vindicated after the telecommunications council said it would renew the tender for a concession in Zagreb.
- Croatia and Yugoslavia begin talks on the missing people from the 1991 conflict.
- Head of the state bank rehabilitation agency, Vladimir Kopf, injured in a car accident.
- Banks discover private citizens as their best partners: Loans to become cheaper and longer.
- Millions may be lost "in the mud" as trade at Croatia's health resorts slips.
- The government proposes a new criminal law, substituting a prison sentence in some cases for public work.
- Economy minister Davor Stern says Croatia must enforce more order in imports to prevent poor quality goods from getting into the country.
- The European Union prepares a technical mission to review Croatia eligibility to aid from the PHARE programme. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
